entities.name: White catfish
entities.fact: The white catfish lives in the brackish tidal rivers of the US east coast and has been introduced to California.

entities.name: Royal pleco
entities.fact: The royal pleco is a South American armoured catfish that rasps wood with its spoon-shaped teeth, helping it digest fibre.

entities.name: Panda corydoras
entities.fact: The panda corydoras, named for its black eye patches and tail spot, comes from the rivers of Peru and is about 5 centimetres long.

entities.name: Bronze corydoras
entities.fact: The bronze corydoras can gulp air at the surface and absorb oxygen through its gut when water is poor in oxygen.

entities.name: Peppered corydoras
entities.fact: The peppered corydoras is a mottled South American armoured catfish that has long been a favourite in aquariums.

entities.name: Gilded catfish
entities.fact: The gilded catfish, or dourada, makes one of the longest freshwater migrations known, swimming thousands of kilometres up the Amazon to spawn.

entities.name: Frogmouth catfish
entities.fact: The frogmouth catfish of South Asia has a huge mouth and lies camouflaged in mud, ambushing small fish that pass close by.

entities.name: Asian stinging catfish
entities.fact: The Asian stinging catfish has a long air-breathing sac and venomous pectoral spines that can give a painful sting.

entities.name: Amur catfish
entities.fact: The Amur catfish is a whiskered East Asian predatory catfish that lives in rivers and lakes of Japan, Korea and China.

entities.name: Yellow-edged moray
entities.fact: The yellow-edged moray is a large Indo-Pacific moray, up to about 1.2 metres long, with a yellow rim on its fins.

entities.name: Undulated moray
entities.fact: The undulated moray is a mottled Indo-Pacific moray that hunts mostly at night and can grow to about 1.5 metres.

entities.name: Whitemouth moray
entities.fact: The whitemouth moray is brown with white spots and has a pale inside to its mouth, which gives it its name.

entities.name: Spotted moray
entities.fact: The spotted moray is a Caribbean and western Atlantic moray whose pale body is covered in small dark spots.

entities.name: Viper moray
entities.fact: The viper moray has long, curved, needle-like teeth that stick out even when its mouth is closed.

entities.name: Goldentail moray
entities.fact: The goldentail moray is a small Caribbean moray, about 60 centimetres long, with a dark body speckled with yellow.

entities.name: Moustache conger
entities.fact: The moustache conger is an Indo-Pacific eel named for the whisker-like flaps above its mouth and can grow longer than a metre.

entities.name: Splendid garden eel
entities.fact: Splendid garden eels live in colonies in sandy burrows, rising like a field of stalks to catch plankton and sinking back when threatened.

entities.name: Australian longfin eel
entities.fact: The Australian longfin eel lives in the rivers of eastern Australia and is thought to migrate to the Coral Sea to spawn.

entities.name: Banded snake eel
entities.fact: The banded snake eel mimics the venomous banded sea krait in colour and pattern, and burrows tail-first into sand.

entities.name: Snubnose parasitic eel
entities.fact: The snubnose parasitic eel has been found burrowing into the flesh of other deep-sea fish, though it also scavenges.

entities.name: Rorqual
entities.fact: Rorquals, such as blue and fin whales, have throat pleats that expand to engulf huge mouthfuls of water, and most grow well beyond 8 metres.

entities.name: Pygmy blue whale
entities.fact: The pygmy blue whale of the Indian Ocean and South Pacific is a subspecies of blue whale that still reaches about 21 metres.

entities.name: Antarctic blue whale
entities.fact: The Antarctic blue whale is the largest subspecies of blue whale, reaching up to about 30 metres, and was nearly wiped out by whaling.

entities.name: Apolemia
entities.fact: Apolemia is a stringy siphonophore colony that can stretch to about 30 metres, making it one of the longest animals known.

entities.name: Longbill spearfish
entities.fact: The longbill spearfish is a slender Atlantic billfish built for speed, like its marlin and sailfish relatives.

entities.name: Mediterranean spearfish
entities.fact: The Mediterranean spearfish is a streamlined billfish whose slender build suits fast open-water hunting.

entities.name: Shortraker rockfish
entities.fact: The shortraker rockfish of the North Pacific has been aged at more than 150 years, making it one of the longest-lived fish.

entities.name: Shortspine thornyhead
entities.fact: The shortspine thornyhead lives deep on the North Pacific slope and can live to over 100 years.

entities.name: Pacific ocean perch
entities.fact: The Pacific ocean perch can live to about 90 years or more and takes many years to reach breeding age.

entities.name: Gold coral
entities.fact: Deep-sea gold corals have been dated at over 2,700 years old, among the oldest living things on Earth.

entities.name: Sinarapan
entities.fact: The sinarapan of the Philippines is one of the smallest fish known, reaching only about 1.2 centimetres in length.

entities.name: Emerald dwarf danio
entities.fact: The emerald dwarf danio of Myanmar's Inle Lake grows to only about 2 to 3 centimetres.

entities.name: Spotted blue-eye
entities.fact: The spotted blue-eye is a small rainbowfish from northern Australia and New Guinea that stays under about 3.5 centimetres.

entities.name: Pygmy killifish
entities.fact: The pygmy killifish of the south-eastern United States rarely grows beyond about 3 to 4 centimetres.

entities.name: Barrier Reef anemonefish
entities.fact: The Barrier Reef anemonefish lives in sea anemones on Australia's reefs and is a close relative of the orange clownfish.

entities.name: Orange skunk clownfish
entities.fact: The orange skunk clownfish has a single white stripe down its back, like a skunk's, and lives in anemones.

entities.name: Seychelles anemonefish
entities.fact: The Seychelles anemonefish is found only around the Seychelles, Mauritius and nearby Indian Ocean islands.

entities.name: Madagascar anemonefish
entities.fact: The Madagascar anemonefish is a clownfish found around Madagascar and the Comoros.

entities.name: Chagos anemonefish
entities.fact: The Chagos anemonefish is a clownfish named for the Chagos Archipelago in the Indian Ocean.

entities.name: Maldive anemonefish
entities.fact: The Maldive anemonefish is a clownfish found around the Maldives and Sri Lanka.

entities.name: Azure damselfish
entities.fact: The azure damselfish has a vivid blue body with a yellow tail and a small size of about 7 centimetres.

entities.name: Blackbar devil
entities.fact: The blackbar devil has a dark bar across its pale body, and it farms algae on the coral it defends.

entities.name: Reticulate dascyllus
entities.fact: The reticulate dascyllus is a small damselfish that shelters among branching corals in large groups.

entities.name: Lemon damselfish
entities.fact: The lemon damselfish is a bright yellow damselfish that lives in branching coral on Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Staghorn damselfish
entities.fact: The staghorn damselfish is a greenish damselfish with pale bars, named for the staghorn corals it shelters among.

entities.name: Neon damselfish
entities.fact: The neon damselfish is a bright blue and yellow damselfish common on Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Threespot damselfish
entities.fact: The threespot damselfish farms algae gardens on Caribbean reefs and chases away much larger fish.

entities.name: Longfin damselfish
entities.fact: The longfin damselfish is a Caribbean damselfish that defends its small territory of algae-covered reef.

entities.name: Giant damselfish
entities.fact: The giant damselfish is among the largest damselfish, reaching about 30 centimetres in the eastern Pacific.

entities.name: Brown chromis
entities.fact: The brown chromis is a common Caribbean damselfish that feeds in schools on plankton above the reef.

entities.name: Black-axil chromis
entities.fact: The black-axil chromis is a green-blue damselfish that forms big plankton-feeding schools over Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Cocoa damselfish
entities.fact: The cocoa damselfish is a small Caribbean damselfish that is brown as an adult and brightly coloured when young.

entities.name: Sailfin pleco
entities.fact: The sailfin pleco is an armoured South American catfish with a tall sail-like dorsal fin that has become an invasive pest in Florida and Asia.

entities.name: Clown pleco
entities.fact: The clown pleco is a small, orange-banded armoured catfish from Venezuela that rasps and eats sunken wood.

entities.name: Gold nugget pleco
entities.fact: The gold nugget pleco comes from Brazil's Xingu River and is named for the golden spots on its dark body.

entities.name: Cuckoo catfish
entities.fact: The cuckoo catfish of Lake Tanganyika lays its eggs among those of mouthbrooding cichlids, and its young then eat the cichlids' own fry.

entities.name: Shovelnose sorubim
entities.fact: The shovelnose sorubim is a South American catfish with a long, flat, spade-shaped snout.

entities.name: Eel-tailed catfish
entities.fact: The eel-tailed catfish is an Australian freshwater catfish with a tapering tail, and the male guards a nest of gravel.

entities.name: Exclamation point rasbora
entities.fact: The exclamation point rasbora is a tiny South-East Asian fish, about 2 centimetres long, with a dark stripe and spot that look like an exclamation mark.

entities.name: Kubotai rasbora
entities.fact: The Kubotai rasbora is a tiny Thai and Myanmar minnow that reaches only about 2 centimetres.

entities.name: Lemon tetra
entities.fact: The lemon tetra is a small, yellow South American fish that grows to only about 4 centimetres.

entities.name: Yellowhead wrasse
entities.fact: The yellowhead wrasse of the Caribbean changes from a yellow juvenile with a blue stripe to a grey-bodied, yellow-headed adult.

entities.name: Redband parrotfish
entities.fact: The redband parrotfish grazes algae from Caribbean reefs and helps keep coral from being smothered.

entities.name: Striped parrotfish
entities.fact: The striped parrotfish is a common Caribbean parrotfish whose young are striped and whose adults are green and purple.

entities.name: Steephead parrotfish
entities.fact: The steephead parrotfish has a steep forehead and strong beak, and it bites away dead coral as it grazes on algae.

entities.name: Bicolor parrotfish
entities.fact: The bicolor parrotfish changes from a pale juvenile to a green and pink adult, and big males grow a bump on the forehead.

entities.name: Clown coris
entities.fact: The clown coris is an Indo-Pacific wrasse; young fish are white-spotted orange, while old males grow a hump on the forehead.

entities.name: Cigar wrasse
entities.fact: The cigar wrasse is a long, slender Indo-Pacific wrasse that can change colour to match seagrass or sand.

entities.name: Saddle wrasse
entities.fact: The saddle wrasse is one of the commonest Hawaiian reef fish and is found only in the Hawaiian islands region.

entities.name: Puddingwife
entities.fact: The puddingwife is a large Atlantic wrasse that can reach about 50 centimetres and changes colour as it matures.

entities.name: Ornate wrasse
entities.fact: The ornate wrasse is a bright Mediterranean wrasse, and many females later change sex to become males.

entities.name: Rainbow wrasse
entities.fact: The rainbow wrasse of the Mediterranean and eastern Atlantic is a small wrasse in which many females later change sex to become brightly striped males.

entities.name: Saddled butterflyfish
entities.fact: The saddled butterflyfish has a big dark patch on its back edged with white, and it is common on Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Pyramid butterflyfish
entities.fact: The pyramid butterflyfish forms big schools that feed on plankton above reef slopes rather than on coral.

entities.name: Chevron butterflyfish
entities.fact: The chevron butterflyfish feeds almost entirely on table corals and defends its coral patch from other fish.

entities.name: Spotfin butterflyfish
entities.fact: The spotfin butterflyfish is a white and yellow Atlantic butterflyfish that grazes on sponges and small invertebrates.

entities.name: Banded butterflyfish
entities.fact: The banded butterflyfish is a Caribbean butterflyfish with black bars that often swims in pairs.

entities.name: Lemonpeel angelfish
entities.fact: The lemonpeel angelfish is a small, bright yellow dwarf angelfish with blue rings around its eyes.

entities.name: Bicolor angelfish
entities.fact: The bicolor angelfish is a small dwarf angelfish, half yellow and half blue, that lives in harems.

entities.name: Blue angelfish
entities.fact: The blue angelfish of the western Atlantic is a large angelfish that can hybridise with the queen angelfish.

entities.name: Majestic angelfish
entities.fact: The majestic angelfish is a blue, yellow and orange Indo-Pacific angelfish that grows to about 25 centimetres.

entities.name: Doctorfish
entities.fact: The doctorfish is a Caribbean surgeonfish that carries a razor-sharp spine near its tail, like a surgeon's scalpel.

entities.name: Ocean surgeonfish
entities.fact: The ocean surgeonfish is a western Atlantic surgeonfish that grazes algae on reefs in large groups.

entities.name: Clown surgeonfish
entities.fact: The clown surgeonfish is striped in blue and yellow and fiercely defends its algae patch with a razor-sharp tail spine.

entities.name: Orangeshoulder tang
entities.fact: The orangeshoulder tang has an orange patch behind its eye and grazes algae in large schools on Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Yellowfin grouper
entities.fact: The yellowfin grouper is a big western Atlantic grouper that can grow to about a metre and can carry ciguatera toxin.

entities.name: Scamp
entities.fact: The scamp is a western Atlantic grouper that begins life as a female and some change sex to become male.

entities.name: Graysby
entities.fact: The graysby is a small Caribbean grouper, about 30 centimetres long, covered in dark spots, and it hides in reef crevices.

entities.name: Rock hind
entities.fact: The rock hind is a small, spotted grouper of the Atlantic that lives in rocky areas and can change colour.

entities.name: Squaretail coralgrouper
entities.fact: The squaretail coralgrouper gathers in large spawning aggregations at certain places in the Indo-Pacific.

entities.name: Brown-marbled grouper
entities.fact: The brown-marbled grouper is a large, marbled Indo-Pacific grouper that can reach about a metre.

entities.name: Peacock hind
entities.fact: The peacock hind is a blue-spotted Indo-Pacific grouper that was introduced to Hawaii to boost fisheries.

entities.name: Dog snapper
entities.fact: The dog snapper is a large Atlantic snapper with prominent canine teeth and a pale triangle below the eye.

entities.name: Red emperor
entities.fact: The red emperor is a large, red Indo-Pacific snapper that can reach about a metre.

entities.name: Humpback red snapper
entities.fact: The humpback red snapper is a snapper with a forked tail and a hump on its forehead, found in groups on Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Barred sand bass
entities.fact: The barred sand bass is a California sea bass popular with anglers and known for gathering to spawn each summer.

entities.name: Butter hamlet
entities.fact: The butter hamlet is a small yellow Caribbean sea bass, and hamlets are unusual in acting as both male and female during spawning.

entities.name: Great seahorse
entities.fact: The great seahorse is one of the biggest seahorses, growing to about 28 centimetres in Indo-Pacific waters.

entities.name: Barbour's seahorse
entities.fact: Barbour's seahorse is a spiny Southeast Asian seahorse named for the American zoologist Thomas Barbour.

entities.name: Crowned seahorse
entities.fact: The crowned seahorse of Japan and Korea has a distinctive crown-like projection on top of its head.

entities.name: Coleman's pygmy seahorse
entities.fact: Coleman's pygmy seahorse is a tiny seahorse, under 3 centimetres long, found in the western Pacific.

entities.name: Severn's pygmy seahorse
entities.fact: Severn's pygmy seahorse is a tiny pygmy seahorse only about 2.5 centimetres long.

entities.name: Broad-nosed pipefish
entities.fact: The broad-nosed pipefish lives in eelgrass of the north-east Atlantic, and the male carries the eggs in a brood pouch.

entities.name: Straight-nosed pipefish
entities.fact: The straight-nosed pipefish is a thin, snake-like pipefish of European seas, and the male glues the eggs to the outside of his belly.

entities.name: Worm pipefish
entities.fact: The worm pipefish is a short, thin pipefish that lives among seaweed on rocky shores around Europe.

entities.name: Dusky pipefish
entities.fact: The dusky pipefish lives in seagrass beds of the western Atlantic and, like seahorses, the male broods the eggs.

entities.name: Bluestripe pipefish
entities.fact: The bluestripe pipefish is a cleaner pipefish that sets up stations on Indo-Pacific reefs and picks parasites off other fish.

entities.name: Robust ghost pipefish
entities.fact: The robust ghost pipefish mimics a drifting leaf or seagrass blade, and the female, not the male, carries the eggs.

entities.name: Ribboned pipehorse
entities.fact: The ribboned pipehorse is an Australian relative of seahorses with a horse-like head and a straight, ribbon-shaped body.

entities.name: Messmate pipefish
entities.fact: The messmate pipefish is a slender, banded pipefish of Indo-Pacific reefs and sandy flats.

entities.name: Flagtail pipefish
entities.fact: The flagtail pipefish has a bold, fan-shaped tail and often lives in caves and crevices of Indo-Pacific reefs.

entities.name: Pipehorse
entities.fact: Pipehorses, relatives of seahorses and pipefish, have a horse-like head on a long straight body and a grasping tail.

entities.name: Checkered puffer
entities.fact: The checkered puffer is a western Atlantic puffer with a checkered back that lives in mangroves and seagrass.

entities.name: Fahaka puffer
entities.fact: The fahaka puffer is a large African freshwater puffer found in the Nile and other rivers, up to about 43 centimetres long.

entities.name: Black triggerfish
entities.fact: The black triggerfish forms big groups that feed on plankton above tropical reefs in all oceans.

entities.name: Ocean triggerfish
entities.fact: The ocean triggerfish is a pelagic triggerfish often found under floating objects far from land.

entities.name: Starry triggerfish
entities.fact: The starry triggerfish is a white-spotted Indo-Pacific triggerfish that lives over sandy and rubble bottoms.

entities.name: Planehead filefish
entities.fact: The planehead filefish is a western Atlantic filefish that can change its colour pattern to blend in.

entities.name: Pinktail triggerfish
entities.fact: The pinktail triggerfish is a dark Indo-Pacific triggerfish with a pink tail, found on outer reef slopes.

entities.name: Bluethroat triggerfish
entities.fact: The bluethroat triggerfish is a small triggerfish with a blue throat, found on deeper reefs of the Indo-Pacific.

entities.name: Thornback cowfish
entities.fact: The thornback cowfish has a rigid boxy shell with horns and spines, protecting it from predators.

entities.name: Tufted puffin
entities.fact: The tufted puffin of the North Pacific has golden head plumes in summer and dives for fish, carrying several crosswise in its bill.

entities.name: Horned puffin
entities.fact: The horned puffin of the North Pacific has a small fleshy 'horn' above each eye and catches small fish underwater.

entities.name: Rhinoceros auklet
entities.fact: The rhinoceros auklet grows a pale horn on its bill in the breeding season and carries fish back to its burrow at night.

entities.name: Black guillemot
entities.fact: The black guillemot is a black seabird with white wing patches and bright red feet that catches fish near the seabed.

entities.name: Northern fulmar
entities.fact: The northern fulmar eats fish, squid and scraps, and spits out foul-smelling stomach oil at intruders.

entities.name: Red-footed booby
entities.fact: The red-footed booby is the smallest booby, with red feet, and it catches flying fish and squid far out at sea.

entities.name: Masked booby
entities.fact: The masked booby plunge-dives into the sea from a height to catch fish and flying fish.

entities.name: Great cormorant
entities.fact: The great cormorant dives after fish, and because its feathers soak up water it perches with wings spread to dry.

entities.name: European shag
entities.fact: The European shag dives for sand eels and other fish, often to depths of tens of metres off rocky coasts.

entities.name: Caspian tern
entities.fact: The Caspian tern, with a heavy red bill, is the largest tern and plunge-dives for fish on coasts and large lakes.

entities.name: Royal tern
entities.fact: The royal tern is a large crested tern that plunge-dives to catch small fish off warm coasts.

entities.name: Black-browed albatross
entities.fact: The black-browed albatross has a dark smudge above each eye and a wingspan of about 2.2 metres, and it feeds on fish, squid and krill.

entities.name: Red-billed tropicbird
entities.fact: The red-billed tropicbird has two very long tail streamers and plunge-dives far out at sea for flying fish and squid.

entities.name: Cape gannet
entities.fact: The Cape gannet breeds on islands off southern Africa and plunge-dives for sardines and anchovies.

entities.name: Humboldt penguin
entities.fact: The Humboldt penguin lives along the cold Humboldt Current coasts of Peru and Chile and hunts anchovies and sardines.

entities.name: Peruvian pelican
entities.fact: The Peruvian pelican feeds mainly on anchoveta in the cold, productive Humboldt Current.

entities.name: Short-beaked echidna
entities.fact: The short-beaked echidna has electroreceptors in its snout that detect the weak electrical signals of its insect prey.

entities.name: Gymnarchus
entities.fact: Gymnarchus, an African freshwater fish, makes weak electric pulses and senses their distortion to find its way and prey in murky water.

entities.name: Brown ghost knifefish
entities.fact: The brown ghost knifefish makes a continuous weak electric field and uses it to navigate and communicate in the dark.

entities.name: Atlantic pomfret
entities.fact: The Atlantic pomfret is an open-ocean fish that migrates over long distances through the North Atlantic.

entities.name: Snake mackerel
entities.fact: The snake mackerel is a long, slim, fanged predator of the open tropical ocean that rises toward the surface at night.

entities.name: Sharptail mola
entities.fact: The sharptail mola is a relative of the ocean sunfish that has a pointed tail lobe and wanders the open ocean.

entities.name: Rainbow runner
entities.fact: The rainbow runner is a fast, streamlined jack that roams the open tropical oceans in schools.

entities.name: Oilfish
entities.fact: The oilfish is a deep, open-ocean predator whose flesh is rich in indigestible wax esters, which can upset the stomach.

entities.name: Antarctic tern
entities.fact: The Antarctic tern nests on coasts around Antarctica and nearby islands and dives for small fish and krill.

entities.name: Kelp gull
entities.fact: The kelp gull is a black-backed gull of Southern Hemisphere coasts, including the Antarctic Peninsula.

entities.name: Snowy sheathbill
entities.fact: The snowy sheathbill is a white scavenger with unwebbed feet that steals eggs and food around Antarctic penguin colonies.

entities.name: Imperial shag
entities.fact: The imperial shag, with a blue ring around its eye, nests on Antarctic and subantarctic coasts and dives for fish.

entities.name: Light-mantled albatross
entities.fact: The light-mantled albatross is a slender, grey-backed albatross that glides around the Southern Ocean and even reaches Antarctic coasts.

entities.name: Cape petrel
entities.fact: The cape petrel is a black and white chequered petrel that follows ships and feeds on krill and fish in the Southern Ocean.

entities.name: Marbled rockcod
entities.fact: The marbled rockcod is an Antarctic fish with antifreeze proteins in its blood, heavily overfished in the 1970s.

entities.name: Antarctic scallop
entities.fact: The Antarctic scallop lives on the seabed beneath the ice and can swim by clapping its shell valves.

entities.name: Antarctic limpet
entities.fact: The Antarctic limpet is the commonest limpet on Antarctic shores and grazes algae from rocks.

entities.name: Antarctic sea star
entities.fact: The Antarctic sea star is one of the commonest seabed animals around Antarctica, scavenging and hunting on the cold shelf.

entities.name: Brown skua
entities.fact: The brown skua is a powerful scavenger and predator that steals eggs and chicks and robs other seabirds of fish around the Southern Ocean.

entities.name: Antarctic giant isopod
entities.fact: The Antarctic giant isopod is a relative of the woodlouse that crawls the cold seabed and can grow to about 20 centimetres.

entities.name: Mangrove tree crab
entities.fact: The mangrove tree crab climbs the roots and branches of mangroves, where it feeds on leaves.

entities.name: Mangrove horseshoe crab
entities.fact: The mangrove horseshoe crab lives in the muddy estuaries and mangroves of South-East Asia and has a round-sectioned tail.

entities.name: Pseudo-nitzschia
entities.fact: Pseudo-nitzschia is a chain-forming diatom, and some species make the toxin domoic acid, which can poison shellfish and seabirds.

entities.name: Karenia brevis
entities.fact: Karenia brevis is the microscopic dinoflagellate behind Florida's red tides and produces toxins that kill fish.

entities.name: Alexandrium
entities.fact: Alexandrium is a dinoflagellate genus whose blooms make saxitoxin, causing paralytic shellfish poisoning.

entities.name: Oithona
entities.fact: Oithona is a tiny copepod, about a millimetre long, and one of the most abundant animals in the sea.

entities.name: Synechococcus
entities.fact: Synechococcus is a tiny photosynthetic bacterium, only about a micrometre wide, that is abundant across the oceans.

entities.name: Ostreococcus
entities.fact: Ostreococcus is a green alga less than a micrometre wide, among the smallest known free-living cells with a nucleus.

entities.name: Ceratium
entities.fact: Ceratium is a dinoflagellate with long horn-like projections, which help it float and deter grazers.

entities.name: Chaetoceros
entities.fact: Chaetoceros is a large genus of diatoms with long spines that link cells into chains and help them float.

entities.name: Sooty gull
entities.fact: The sooty gull is a dark brown-grey gull of the Red Sea and Arabian coasts, where it nests on islands and eats fish.

entities.name: Brown meagre
entities.fact: The brown meagre of the Mediterranean makes loud drumming and grunting sounds with its swim bladder.

entities.name: Meagre
entities.fact: The meagre is a big croaker that forms spawning groups and makes a loud drumming noise, audible from boats.

entities.name: Pigfish
entities.fact: The pigfish makes grunting noises by grinding its throat teeth, which gives it its name.

entities.name: Spot
entities.fact: The spot is a small croaker of the US east coast with a dark shoulder spot, and like other croakers it can drum.

entities.name: Northern searobin
entities.fact: The northern searobin makes croaking and grunting sounds by drumming muscles against its swim bladder.

entities.name: Great Meteor Seamount
entities.fact: The Great Meteor Seamount is a flat-topped underwater mountain in the north-east Atlantic, whose summit lies a few hundred metres below the surface.

entities.name: Tri-spine horseshoe crab
entities.fact: The tri-spine horseshoe crab of Asian coasts belongs to a lineage that has barely changed in hundreds of millions of years.

entities.name: Green sturgeon
entities.fact: The green sturgeon of the North Pacific is a bony-plated fish from a lineage dating back to the age of the dinosaurs.

entities.name: Topsmelt
entities.fact: The topsmelt is a small silverside that schools in bays and estuaries of the American Pacific coast and is eaten by many predators.

entities.name: Jacksmelt
entities.fact: The jacksmelt is a schooling silverside of the American Pacific coast that grows to about 40 centimetres.

entities.name: Surf smelt
entities.fact: The surf smelt is a small schooling fish that spawns on gravel beaches in the North Pacific and feeds salmon and seabirds.

entities.name: Cape anchovy
entities.fact: The Cape anchovy is the key forage fish of southern Africa's Benguela upwelling system, feeding penguins, gannets and predatory fish.

entities.name: Argentine anchovy
entities.fact: The Argentine anchovy schools in vast numbers off Argentina, Uruguay and southern Brazil.

entities.name: Araucanian herring
entities.fact: The Araucanian herring is a small schooling fish of the Chilean coast that supports a large fishery.

entities.name: Starlet sea anemone
entities.fact: The starlet sea anemone is a small estuarine anemone used in research because it can regrow a whole body from a cut piece.

entities.name: Vase tunicate
entities.fact: The vase tunicate can regrow its lost siphons and parts of its body, which makes it a favourite for regeneration studies.

entities.name: Three-banded panther worm
entities.fact: The three-banded panther worm, a small acoel flatworm, can regrow an entire new body from a fragment.
